clinician.trajectory_summary: A 29-year-old female presented with a 2-year history of intermittent respiratory symptoms (cough, sputum) following COVID-19 infection during an outbreak, for which she was treated with Panadol Extra, antibiotics, and steroids with only partial improvement. Due to persistence of symptoms, a high-resolution CT scan of the chest was performed, which revealed an irregular pulmonary opacity in the right lower lobe with central fluid attenuation, initially suspected to be an abscess or less likely a pulmonary neoplasm. Fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) was performed on the right hemithorax in a prone position, which suggested the presence of a hydatid cyst (HC). Subsequently, thoracotomy was performed and the abscess/cyst was surgically removed. Histopathological examination of the resected specimen confirmed the diagnosis of hydatid cyst disease (echinococcosis). The post-operative period was uneventful, and the patient's symptoms improved.
